question: Which combination represents the minimum standard monitoring required during general anaesthesia?

answers.text: Pulse oximetry and non-invasive blood pressure only

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: These two alone are insufficient. End-tidal CO₂ monitoring (capnography) is mandatory during any general anaesthetic with an endotracheal tube or LMA to confirm correct airway placement and detect hypo- or hyperventilation.

answers.text: Pulse oximetry, non-invasive blood pressure, ECG, and end-tidal CO₂

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The minimum standard anaesthetic monitoring includes: SpO₂ (pulse oximetry), NIBP, ECG, and EtCO₂ (capnography). Temperature monitoring is added for procedures >30 minutes.
An arterial line is invasive and not part of minimum routine monitoring; pulse oximetry is essential but missing here.

answers.text: Pulse oximetry, EtCO₂, BIS (bispectral index), and arterial line

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: BIS and arterial lines are useful in specific contexts but are not minimum standard for all GA cases; ECG and NIBP are essential and missing here.

overallFeedback.feedback: The minimum standard monitoring for GA is: SpO₂ (pulse oximetry), NIBP, ECG, and end-tidal CO₂. Capnography is mandatory — it is the most sensitive early indicator of oesophageal intubation.
Well done. SpO₂ + NIBP + ECG + EtCO₂ are the four cornerstones of intraoperative monitoring for every general anaesthetic.
